put.summary: Modify a single occurrence of a recurring assignm…
put.description: Update a single occurrence of a recurring assignment, splitting it off from the series as a one-off while leaving every other occurrence unchanged. Identify the occurrence with `original_starts_at` (its original scheduled start time in the series, which does not change even if the occurrence was previously moved). The `id` path parameter must be the series' ancestor assignment. The request is idempotent - repeating it for the same occurrence updates the existing one-off instead of creating a duplicate.

address.description: The address where the assignment takes place. Pass null to clear it.

activity_id.description: The ID of the activity the assignment is for.

work_order_id.description: The ID of the work order the assignment is associated with.

equipment_ids.description: IDs of equipment assigned to the assignment.

certification_type_ids.description: IDs of certification types required for the assignment.

rate_differential_id.description: The ID of the rate differential applied to the assignment.

custom_color.description: An optional color override used when rendering the assignment.

starts_at.description: When the assignment starts, as an ISO-8601 datetime (UTC).

ends_at.description: When the assignment ends, as an ISO-8601 datetime (UTC).

original_starts_at.description: The occurrence's original scheduled start time within the recurring series, as an ISO-8601 datetime (UTC). This identifies which occurrence to edit and is stable even if the occurrence was previously moved - always pass the series' scheduled slot time (as returned by list occurrences), not the occurrence's current start. The rest of the series is left unchanged.

get.summary: List the occurrences of a recurring assignment
get.description: Expand a recurring assignment into its individual occurrences over a date window. Recurring occurrences are generated from the series' recurrence rule and are not stored individually, so use this endpoint to discover an occurrence's start time before editing it with `PUT /assignments/{id}/modify_occurrence`. The `id` path parameter must be the series' ancestor assignment. The window is required and cannot exceed 366 days.

team_member_id.description: The ID of the team member this reimbursement is for.

date.description: The date the expense was incurred, as an ISO-8601 date string.

type.description: The type of reimbursement. `payroll_correction` is system-generated and cannot be written.

amount.description: The amount of the reimbursement (in dollars). Required for `out_of_pocket`. Computed from mileage details for `mileage`.

is_taxable.description: Whether the reimbursement is taxable. Defaults from the category when omitted. Only honored when `payout_method` is `payroll`; otherwise stored as false.

vendor_name.description: The name of the vendor. Required for `out_of_pocket` reimbursements.

tax.description: The tax amount included in the reimbursement (in dollars).

payout_method.description: How the reimbursement is paid out. Defaults from the category, then payroll/ACH/manual.

file_ids.description: IDs of files (e.g., receipts) attached to the reimbursement.

job_id.description: The ID of the job assigned to the reimbursement.

activity_id.description: The ID of the activity assigned to the reimbursement.

cost_type_id.description: The ID of the cost type assigned to the reimbursement.

class_id.description: The ID of the class assigned to the reimbursement.

location_id.description: The ID of the location assigned to the reimbursement.

department_id.description: The ID of the department assigned to the reimbursement.

company_entity_id.description: The ID of the company entity assigned to the reimbursement.

expense_account_id.description: The ID of the ledger account the reimbursement is booked to.

expense_reimbursement_category_id.description: The ID of the expense reimbursement category. Category defaults (including taxability) apply when this is set.

mileage_detail.description: Mileage details. Required for `type: mileage` reimbursements.

trip.description: Ordered list of stops on the trip. Each stop requires a place ID and description.

place_id.description: Google Maps place ID for the location.

description.description: Human-readable description of the location (e.g., a street address).

rate_snapshot.description: The mileage rate (in dollars per mile) used to compute the reimbursement amount.

commute_deduction.description: Whether the team member's commute miles are deducted from the trip distance, and how. `one_way` subtracts the one-way commute; `round_trip` subtracts double. Null/undefined means no deduction.

custom_fields.description: Custom field values to set on the reimbursement.

post.summary: Transfer a team member to a different entity
post.description: Move a team member from one entity to another, with options to transfer benefits as well as reassigning their workplace and pay schedule. If your company uses Employee Navigator, you must first move the team member to the correct subscriber group in Employee Navigator before transferring. If your company uses a Miter Benefits Administration, Miter will move the team member to the new company entity but you will need to manually transfer or end-date Miter Benefits Administration-managed benefits. Non-managed benefits will still be transferred if the transfer option is enabled.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: POST /team_members/:id/change_entity Parameter

note.description: An optional note to accompany the transfer, explaining why the transfer was made.

benefits.description: Whether to transfer existing benefits to the new entity along with the team member. If your company uses Employee Navigator, you must first move the team member to the correct subscriber group in Employee Navigator before transferring in Miter. If your company uses Miter Benefits Administration, Miter will move the team member to the new company entity, but you will need to manually transfer or end-date Miter Benefits Administration-managed benefits. Benefits managed through the Miter Benefits Administration broker console or Employee Navigator will be automatically skipped during transfer. Non-managed benefits (e.g., 401k plans not managed through the Miter Benefits Administration broker console or Employee Navigator) will still be transferred. Set to true to transfer non-managed benefits, or false to end-date benefits without transferring.

workplace_id.description: The ID of the workplace to transfer the team member to after the transfer.

pay_schedule_id.description: The ID of the pay schedule to transfer the team member to after the transfer.

prevent_time_type_downgrades.description: When true, no threshold may lower a team member's time type during a day; once hours reach `overtime` or `double_overtime` classification, they cannot be reclassified to a lower tier. Because hours-worked thresholds count the hours actually paid at each earning type, a suppressed downgrade keeps feeding the count that unlocks the next threshold — and an earning type the team member has moved above stops counting up, which can put a threshold needing more of those hours permanently out of reach.

current_pay_rate_group_version_id.description: The ID of the pay rate group version that is currently effective.

team_member_id.description: The team member id for this pay rate.

pay_type.description: Whether this is a hourly or salary pay rate.

apply_allowances.description: Whether allowance earnings were added to the payroll.

apply_fringes.description: Whether fringe earnings were added to the payroll.

ignore_time_off_requests.description: Whether time off requests in the pay period were left out of the payroll.

force_supplemental_withholding.description: Whether earnings on the payroll are taxed at the supplemental withholding rate.

apply_benefits.description: Whether benefit deductions and contributions are applied to the payroll.

apply_post_tax_deductions.description: Whether post-tax deductions are applied to the payroll.

PayrollPaymentBenefit.description: A single benefit line on the payment.

type.description: The kind of benefit. Known values include `401k`, `125_medical`, `hsa`.

description.description: A human-readable name for the benefit.

employee_contribution_amount.description: The amount the team member contributed.

PayrollPaymentEarning.description: A single earning line on the payment.

id.description: The ID of the earning line.

category.description: Why Miter created this earning. Use `pay_type` for how it is taxed. `check_created` earnings were added by the payroll processor rather than by Miter. Null on historical earnings whose category this API version does not model.

pay_type.description: How the earning is classified for pay and tax purposes. Null on historical earnings whose pay type this API version does not model.

description.description: A description of the earning.

date.description: The date the earning was worked or applied.

hours.description: The hours the earning covers. Null on earnings that are not hours-based.

amount.description: The amount of the earning, rounded so that a paystub's line amounts sum to its gross pay.

hourly_rates.description: The hourly rates the earning was paid at. Null on earnings that are not hours-based.

regular_rate_of_pay.description: The blended straight-time rate used to derive overtime premiums for the workweek this earning falls in.

custom_earning_code_id.description: The ID of the custom earning code applied to the earning.

timesheet_id.description: The ID of the timesheet whose hours produced this earning.

job_id.description: The ID of the job the earning is costed to.

activity_id.description: The ID of the activity (cost code) the earning is costed to.

department_id.description: The ID of the department the earning is costed to.

location_id.description: The ID of the location the earning is costed to.

class_id.description: The ID of the class the earning is costed to.

ledger_account_id.description: The ID of the ledger account the earning posts to.

workers_compensation_code_id.description: The ID of the workers' compensation code the earning is classified under.

equipment_ids.description: The IDs of the equipment operated while earning this line.

quantity_log_id.description: The ID of the quantity log that produced this piece-rate earning.

time_off_request_id.description: The ID of the time off request this earning pays out.

time_off_policy_id.description: The ID of the time off policy this earning draws against.

expense_reimbursement_id.description: The ID of the expense reimbursement this earning pays out.

PayrollPaymentHourlyRates.description: The hourly rates the earning was paid at.

PayrollPaymentPostTaxDeduction.description: A single post-tax deduction line on the payment.

type.description: The kind of post-tax deduction. Known values include `child_support`, `miscellaneous`.

description.description: A human-readable name for the deduction.

amount.description: The amount deducted after taxes.

PayrollPaymentRefund.description: A direct deposit that could not be delivered and was returned, to be reissued as a paper check.

amount.description: The amount refunded.

refunded_at.description: When the refund occurred, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

PayrollPaymentReimbursement.description: A single reimbursement line on the payment.

id.description: The ID of the reimbursement line.

amount.description: The amount reimbursed. Reimbursements are not taxed.

description.description: A description of the reimbursement.

date.description: The date the reimbursement applies to.

job_id.description: The ID of the job the reimbursement is costed to.

activity_id.description: The ID of the activity (cost code) the reimbursement is costed to.

ledger_account_id.description: The ID of the ledger account the reimbursement posts to.

expense_reimbursement_id.description: The ID of the expense reimbursement this line pays out.

payroll_id.description: The ID of the payroll run this payment belongs to.

company_entity_id.description: The ID of the company entity that paid this payment. Null on old payments the multi-entity backfill could not map to an entity.

pay_schedule_id.description: The ID of the pay schedule the payroll ran on. Null for off-cycle payrolls.

team_member_id.description: The ID of the team member who was paid.

payment_type.description: Whether the team member was paid as an employee (taxes withheld) or as a contractor (gross, no withholding).

payroll_type.description: The type of payroll this payment rode on. `historical` payments record pay from before the company moved to Miter.

status.description: Where the payment is in its lifecycle, mirroring its payroll. `paid` means the money went out.

pay_frequency.description: How often the payroll's pay schedule pays out.

period_start.description: The first day of the pay period the payment covers.

period_end.description: The last day of the pay period the payment covers.

payday.description: The date the team member was paid.

payment_reference.description: A short Miter-generated identifier for this payment. Appears on certified payroll reports and as the check voucher number in accounting exports.

paper_check_number.description: The paper check number, when the payment was delivered by paper check.

gross_pay.description: Total taxable and non-taxable earnings before deductions, excluding imputed earnings and reimbursements.

net_pay.description: Take-home pay after taxes, benefits, and deductions. Null until the payroll has been calculated.

reimbursement_total.description: Total reimbursements paid on this payment. Reimbursements are not taxed.

is_void.description: Whether this payment is the reversing entry that voids another payment, rather than an original payment.

voided.description: Whether this payment was voided. The reversing entry is a separate payment with `is_void` set to true.

void_requested.description: Whether a void was requested for this payment but has not finished processing.

ach_reversal_reason.description: Why the direct deposit for this payment was reversed.

corrected_by_payment_id.description: The ID of the payment that replaced this one after it was voided. Null when this payment was not corrected.

paid_time_off_balance_hours.description: The team member's paid time off balance after this payment was applied.

sick_balance_hours.description: The team member's sick time balance after this payment was applied.

earnings.description: The earning lines that make up this payment's gross pay.

reimbursements.description: The reimbursement lines on this payment.

taxes.description: The tax lines on this payment, both employee-withheld and employer-paid. Empty for contractor payments and until the payroll has been calculated.

benefits.description: The benefit contributions on this payment. Empty for contractor payments.

time_off_logs.description: Time off accrued, used, and paid out on this payment, broken out by policy.

refunds.description: Direct deposits on this payment that were returned undelivered.

new_balance_hours.description: The policy balance after this payment was applied.

type.description: What the warning is about. Known values include `unhandled_fringe_deduction`, `negative_net_pay`.

text.description: A human-readable explanation of the warning.

expected_amount.description: The amount that would have applied had the warning's condition not occurred.

payday_notification_sent.description: Whether the payday notification has been sent to the team members on the payroll.

payday_notifications_enabled.description: Whether payday notifications are turned on for this payroll.

time_off_balances_updated.description: Whether time off balances have been updated to reflect the time off paid on the payroll.

totals.description: Monetary totals for the payroll. Null until the payroll has been calculated.

For timesheets pulled from Procore into Miter, this is the source timecard entry the timesheet was created from (one-to-one). For timesheets Miter pushes to Procore, it is the primary entry, with the full per-earning-type set in `timecard_entry_ids`.

timecard_entry_ids.description: IDs of the Procore timecard entries created when Miter pushes this timesheet to Procore — one per earning type (regular/overtime/double overtime), so a single timesheet maps to many. Not populated for timesheets pulled from Procore into Miter; use `timecard_entry_id` there.

time_bill_external_ids.description: External IDs of the NetSuite time bills created for this timesheet when syncing earnings as timesheets.

work_order_id.description: The ID of the work order this timesheet is associated with. Fetch valid IDs from GET /work_orders. When the work order is linked to a job, Miter forces the timesheet onto that job: submitting a different job_id returns a 400, and omitting job_id fills it in from the work order. Set to null to clear.

workers_compensation_code_id.description: The ID of the workers' compensation code set directly on this timesheet. Fetch valid IDs from GET /workers_comp_codes; submitting an ID that does not exist in your company returns a 404. When set, it takes precedence over the code Miter would otherwise derive at payroll time from the activity, classification, job, or team member. Set to null to clear.

notes.description: Optional notes attached to the timesheet.

custom_id.description: The customer-supplied stable identifier for this timesheet. Used to deduplicate upserts

earning_type.description: The REG/OT/DOT earning classification for this timesheet. This field is null until the timesheet is paid and Miter applies OT/DOT rules, unless it was explicitly set during creation or update. For company-specific earning codes, see custom_earning_code_id.

custom_earning_code_id.description: The ID of a custom earning code to apply to this timesheet. Fetch valid codes from GET /custom_earning_codes. Use this field for company-specific earning classifications; earning_type controls REG/OT/DOT classification and accepts only hourly, overtime, or double_overtime.

time_off_policy_id.description: For policy-scoped time off earning types (`pto`, `sick`), the ID of the time off policy that governs this earning. Null for standard earning types or when no governing policy is recorded.

custom_field_values.description: Custom field values on the timesheet.

crew_ids.description: The IDs of the crews the team member belonged to when this timesheet was recorded. Snapshotted at creation and re-cached when the team member changes, so historical timesheets stay associated with the crew they were worked under even after the team member moves to a different crew.

current_break_policy_id.description: The break policy that currently governs this timesheet. Derived at read time from the timesheet's team member, job, department, and location assignments (not stored), so it always reflects the current policy configuration. Null when no break policy governs the timesheet — either your company does not use break policies (company-level break types from GET /break-types apply) or none resolves for this timesheet (no itemized break types apply). Otherwise, a break type from GET /break-types is valid here only when its break_policy_id equals this value.

classification_id.description: The classification set on this timesheet, overriding the one Miter would otherwise derive from the activity, job, pay rate group, and team member. Null when none is set; see classification_excluded. Fetch valid IDs from GET /pay_rate_groups/{pay_rate_group_id}/classifications.

classification_excluded.description: True when this timesheet is deliberately marked as having no classification, so Miter derives none. When false and classification_id is null, Miter derives the classification.

standard_classification_id.description: The standard classification set directly on this timesheet. Takes precedence over the team member's standard classification when Miter resolves a pay rate within a pay rate group. Fetch valid IDs from GET /standard_classifications.
